defects.title: is_service_role() / raw != NULL-collapse authorization pattern — 4-file audit, 2 live exploits found and fixed
defects.detail: public.is_service_role() returns SQL NULL (not false) when neither JWT claim is set, and a raw `auth.uid() != p_user_id` guard evaluates NULL for any unauthenticated (anon) caller — both collapse a NOT-wrapped AND-chain guard to NULL, which PL/pgSQL's IF treats as false, silently bypassing the RAISE EXCEPTION. Live audit of the LIVE function definitions (not migration-file text) across all 4 originally-flagged files found: (1) get_referral_stats — migration text vulnerable but superseded by a later migration using IS DISTINCT FROM, and anon has no EXECUTE grant anyway — CLEAN, no action. (2) get_user_activation_score — had a prior partial fix (COALESCE around is_service_role) but still carried the raw auth.uid() != p_user_id leading term, and anon DOES have EXECUTE — CONFIRMED LIVE EXPLOITABLE via direct curl (HTTP 200, real data, arbitrary UUID, zero auth) — FIXED. (3) get_user_engagement_stats — fully unpatched, anon-executable — CONFIRMED LIVE EXPLOITABLE the same way — FIXED. Both fixes applied via migration 20260822225616 (IS DISTINCT FROM + COALESCE), re-verified with a second identical curl showing HTTP 400 Access denied post-fix.
defects.next_action: Fix applied to live production DB, verified, and the migration file committed/pushed via PR #49. Only remaining lower-priority follow-on: sweep the rest of the schema for any other raw `auth.uid() != ...` or unwrapped `is_service_role()` guards outside this specific 4-file list — not yet done.

defects.title: CONFIRMED: frontend Vercel deploy pipeline has been blocked for 23+ commits — production frontend is running stale, pre-break code
defects.detail: Reclassified up from P1 after item 4's investigation replaced inference with proof. Root cause is no longer ambiguous: every commit since b7a5068e (23 commits, HEAD=8b7faf11) fails the GitHub 'Vercel' status check with an explicit message -- 'Git author AIWMCX must have access to the project on Vercel to create deployments' (target_url is a live Vercel team-invite link for team jeltovbogdan-7049's projects). The last SUCCESSFUL deploy (741bbbe7) was authored by gpt-engineer-app[bot]; every commit since was authored as AIWMCX, which the invite link itself confirms lacks Vercel team membership -- Vercel's Deployment Protection blocks git-triggered deploys from non-team-member authors by design. Directly proved with the live bundle: fetched https://www.aiwmcquantis.com's current JS asset and grepped it -- 0 matches for claim_content_admin_if_allowlisted/isContentAdmin/requireContentAdmin (the content_admin feature shipped in PR #47, commit 20ff6af2, earlier this same session), but 1 match for the OLD claim_admin_if_allowlisted and 16 matches for OLD requireAdmin. The live frontend is unambiguously the pre-b7a5068e build. Full evidence and required-action detail in docs/VERCEL_DEPLOY_PIPELINE_FINDING.md.
defects.next_action: 3 viable fixes, in order of discovery: 1) Grant GitHub identity AIWMCX access on the Vercel team via the invite link already present in the GitHub status check target_url (requires the Vercel team owner to act in the Vercel dashboard). 2) Relax Vercel Project Settings -> Git -> Deployment Protection for git-author requirements (same dashboard access needed, weaker security posture). 3) NEW, likely lower-friction: .github/workflows/vercel-production-deploy.yml already exists as a manual one-click CLI-based deploy (VERCEL_TOKEN auth, bypasses the git-author check entirely) with a built-in smoke test + fidelity gate + auto-rollback -- but it has never been run and cannot run yet. Its own scripts/preflight-secrets.sh hard-requires 11 secrets (VERCEL_TOKEN, VERCEL_ORG_ID, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID, SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY); gh secret list shows only CRON_SECRET/SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN/SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD exist, so 9 of the 11 are missing. Provisioning those 9 secrets and running this workflow may resolve the whole defect without any Vercel-team-membership change -- but it is a 9-secret provisioning task, not a 3-secret one. After any fix: force-redeploy main HEAD and re-run the same live-bundle grep to confirm requireContentAdmin/isContentAdmin now appear, then build the frontend build-metadata endpoint (Workstream A) so this stops requiring bundle forensics. Until fixed: PR #47's frontend half (Content Studio/Autoposter access for the 2 newly-granted accounts) is NOT functionally live even though its database grant is -- treat that item as reopened, not done.

defects.title: Analytics parity gap between persisted analyses and completion funnel events — magnitude confirmed real, not fully explained
defects.detail: Two independent measurements, two different rolling windows, both show a real gap: 2026-08-18 measured 11 completion events / 27 analyses (~59% gap) in its 30-day window; this capture measured 30 completion events / 46 analyses (~35% gap) in its own 30-day window. Neither figure supersedes the other -- do not report this as 'the gap improved from 59% to 35%,' that would be comparing two different windows as if they were a trend. The honest finding is: a material, currently-unexplained under-reporting gap exists in every measurement taken.
defects.next_action: Task chip task_46a94f92 already covers the code-path audit (which analysis-creation paths call trackAnalysisCompleted() and which don't) — execute that before drawing further conclusions from either number.

defects.title: Local sitemap.xml rebuild is not byte-reproducible with the CI-produced live sitemap
defects.detail: scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs computes <lastmod> per-route from real git history and falls back to 'today' when no match is found. Rebuilding sitemap.xml locally in this working directory and diffing against the live-downloaded https://www.aiwmcquantis.com/sitemap.xml shows an identical 88-URL set (zero drift, zero apex leakage) but divergent <lastmod>, <priority>, <changefreq>, and route ordering. This is not a live defect — the currently-served sitemap is correct and stable — but it means a local rebuild cannot be used as a predictor/diff baseline for the live artifact in its current form.
defects.next_action: Not urgent. If ever picked up: make lastmod computation environment-independent (e.g. read from a committed content-hash/date map instead of live git-log lookups), or explicitly document that local rebuild is diagnostic-only and never diff it against production.

defects.title: Unsupported/unverified quantitative claim cluster propagated across 7 machine-readable homepage locations
defects.detail: The claim cluster '1,000 Monte Carlo scenarios/simulations', '97,500 [industry] benchmark data points', and 'under 90 seconds' appears in: meta description, og:description, twitter:description, WebPage JSON-LD .description, SoftwareApplication JSON-LD .description, and 2 separate FAQPage JSON-LD answers. One of those FAQ answers additionally claims 'every output includes a confidence score and data quality rating.' None of these figures were evaluated for truth this capture — only enumerated for location and propagation breadth. Because they're embedded in structured data (not just visible copy), they also feed search-engine rich snippets and any AI/LLM answer engine that parses JSON-LD directly.
defects.next_action: Feeds Workstream T (Claim Audit) once started: verify each number against the actual engine/benchmark dataset (e.g. does the benchmark dataset actually contain 97,500 data points; is 1,000 the actual Monte Carlo iteration count; is a 'confidence score and data quality rating' actually rendered anywhere in the product). Fix or substantiate all 7 locations together — a partial fix would leave the claim inconsistent across surfaces.

defects.title: Sentry error tracking (and Replay) is completely dark in the live production build — VITE_SENTRY_DSN unset at build time
defects.detail: src/lib/sentry.ts's initSentry() returns early with console.warn('Sentry DSN not configured - error tracking disabled') whenever import.meta.env.VITE_SENTRY_DSN is falsy. Live-browser console check against https://www.aiwmcquantis.com confirmed this exact warning fires on page load right now -- Sentry.init() is never reached, so NO errors, NO breadcrumbs, and NO session replay are being captured or sent anywhere from production today. Cross-checked against the live JS bundle: it contains general Sentry SDK code (logger, captureException scaffolding) but zero occurrences of maskAllText/blockAllMedia/replayIntegration -- consistent with Rollup dead-code-eliminating the entire Sentry.init(...) block because the DSN constant was empty at build time. This means the privacy-hardening fix applied this pass (maskAllText/blockAllMedia true) is currently inert in production -- there is no active exposure right now, but there was also no error monitoring at all, which is its own gap.
defects.next_action: Requires Vercel project environment-variable configuration (VITE_SENTRY_DSN) -- outside this session's access, same blocker family as QNT-DEFECT-002. Once set and a deploy actually reaches production (contingent on QNT-DEFECT-002 being fixed first), re-run the identical live-console check to confirm Sentry initializes, then re-fetch the live bundle and grep for maskAllText/blockAllMedia to confirm the hardened config (not the old unmasked one) is what actually goes live.
defects.owner: release engineering / observability (blocked on Vercel env-var + deploy access)

defects.title: Full-history gitleaks scan (2916 commits) found 45 raw matches; almost all false-positive, but 2 categories are real secret disclosures needing rotation/acceptance decisions
defects.detail: Ran gitleaks v8.30.1 (downloaded fresh, no prior tooling existed) against the full git history. 45 raw findings: 28 jwt (all decoded to role:anon on either the current project dmlxrvfyqsakyjomsvdj or a retired one gafxacjhkqsdzwwzhbor -- Supabase anon keys are public-by-design, false positives), 15 generic-api-key (11 are Vault secret NAME lookups like 'pii_encryption_key_v2' used in SQL WHERE clauses -- not the secret values -- false positives; 4 are the SAME real hex string 'fbfa43cf0894...' embedded in 3 migration files as the pre-rotation CRON_SECRET, confirmed already rotated/dead per this session's own earlier work AND still present verbatim in the CURRENT tracked migration files, not just history -- migrations are append-only by this repo's own doctrine so these will not be edited, but the value is confirmed non-functional against live cron jobs), 1 curl-auth-header ('YOUR_API_KEY' doc placeholder, false positive), 1 linkedin-client-id ('handleCopyLink' matched inside an old committed .vercel/ build sourcemap, false positive, and .vercel/ is gitignored now). SEPARATELY, and NOT a false positive: .env.md (a currently-tracked reference doc, now containing only placeholders) briefly held real-looking cleartext values for VITE_ADMIN_UPLOAD_KEY, VITE_CRON_SECRET, and VITE_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET across several 2025-11 through 2026-01 commits. Confirmed the real .env (which Vite actually loads) never carried these -- they were never shipped in the public bundle, and repo is PRIVATE, so exposure is limited to repo collaborators, not the public. Live-tested the ADMIN_UPLOAD_KEY value (quantis_admin_7722_xPqq23a544849283484d) via a harmless empty POST to the manage-benchmarks edge function's x-admin-key header (approved by the user after an auto-mode classifier block) -- returned HTTP 401, CONFIRMED DEAD, not the current live secret. STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (whsec_TICzgu3bt7j3rsQy28OYQg9q9035HSDM) could not be safely tested the same way -- doing so would require forging a valid Stripe-signed payload, which is itself simulating an attack and was not attempted.
affected_files: .env.md (current: placeholders only, historical commits had real-looking values)
defects.next_action: 1) Recommend rotating STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the Stripe dashboard purely out of caution, since its historical .env.md value cannot be safely confirmed dead or alive without a Stripe connector this session lacks -- see QNT-DEFECT-009. 2) No action needed on ADMIN_UPLOAD_KEY (confirmed dead) or CRON_SECRET (already rotated and confirmed dead in prior session work) beyond what's already done. 3) Do not edit the historical migration files -- they are append-only by design; the dead secret sitting in them is an accepted, non-exploitable artifact. 4) Gitleaks is now wired into CI (.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml, scoped to new commits only via --log-opts, never full history) with .gitleaks.toml documenting every allowlist decision and why -- this closes the 'Gitleaks not yet installed' gap from Workstream C going forward; it does not retroactively clean history.
